_title: Powers in the home regions: nine powers over six regions where characters come from and nobody held ground
_why: CCODE-483: 30 of 38 regions have no power, including six that characters on this device are from — their codex hears of nothing at home. This fills those six first. Supply lines by the ruled rule (SNG-641 §6), one per Sovereign per region.

added.name: The Unshadowed

contingents.what: zealots who have burned the dark out of themselves, carrying lanterns at noon

holds.name: the burning ring, where the glass is still warm

added.wantsFromYou: Nothing hidden. Open your packs, your doors and your face, and say aloud the thing you would rather not.
added.offersYou: Passage across the glass plain, water where there is none, and the certainty that nothing will ever be kept from you again.
added.leverage: They cannot abide a shadow they did not choose. A shuttered lantern enrages them, and an enraged zealot stops watching the road.
added.whenBroken: The Blaze stops advancing for a season, and in Glasshome people begin to hang curtains, quietly, and do not talk about it.
added.plainly: The zealots who live inside the Blaze. They have burned away everything in themselves that could cast a shadow, and they want to do the same for everyone else.
added.descriptionSeed: The Unshadowed are what the Blaze makes of people who stay in it: a devotion, not a civilization. Valen Sunwrack leads them outward a mile a year, and every village they reach loses its curtains, its locks and its secrets, and calls it dawn.
added.appearance: A glass plain under a white sky, figures in bleached robes carrying lit lanterns in full daylight, a ring of warm glass around a light too bright to look at

feedsGM.through: a light that leaves nothing unseen, carried outward a mile a year

secretsGM: Valen does not know whose line he is (R40b.4). He believes the dawn was his own idea.
The Open Lantern (SNG-642) is carried by their captains.

added.name: The Glass Assembly

contingents.what: lens-guards and beam-wrights of the Lensward

holds.name: the great focusing array on the border

added.wantsFromYou: To know what you are carrying and to be told the truth about it. They will not search you; they will ask, and they will remember the answer.
added.offersYou: Lenses that show a thing as it is, safe passage on the glass plain, and a hearing in a city with no walls to hide a lie behind.
added.leverage: The Assembly meets in the open because Glasshome has no interior walls. Anything said to it is said to the whole city.
added.whenBroken: The Lensward arrays go dark, the border opens, and the Blaze advances on Glasshome with nothing focused against it.

bodies.name: the Glass Assembly
bodies.does: governs Glasshome in the open, where everyone can see

added.plainly: Glasshome's governing assembly. It meets in the open, because the city has no interior walls, and it holds the border against the Blaze with lenses.
added.descriptionSeed: The Glass Assembly governs a city built on the plain the Blaze made, by people the Blaze made, and it spends most of its strength keeping the Blaze from finishing the job. Its arrays at the Lensward focus the light back on itself. It is fair, it is exhausting, and it hears every case in public.
added.appearance: An open hall of clear glass in a city without interior walls, a crowd watching every speaker, the great lens-arrays of the border catching the light beyond

added.name: The High Temple of the Body

contingents.what: temple adepts whose bodies are their discipline

holds.name: the long yard and its bathhouse

added.wantsFromYou: Respect for the body you are in. Train with them for a season, or keep your contempt for flesh off their mountain.
added.offersYou: Training that makes a body answer, healing the flesh does for itself, and adepts who will stand in a line for anyone who stands in theirs.
added.leverage: They will not strike a body that has not been trained to answer. Anyone who comes to the mountain unarmed and untrained is safe on it.
added.whenBroken: The Grindstone empties, the Middle Way loses the half of its balance that was flesh, and the Cogitarium's cold comes down the mountain unopposed.
added.plainly: The temple-order of the Somatic Reaches, where training the body is devotion. It guards the mountain and anyone on it who respects the flesh.
added.descriptionSeed: The High Temple rises a mountain in tiers of training-grounds, and every soul on it hones breath, poise and endurance as worship. Its adepts keep the Grindstone for soldiers who want to be trained properly, and they look down the mountain at the Cogitarium with a grief they rarely say aloud.
added.appearance: Tiered training grounds climbing a mountain, adepts moving in unison at dawn, a long yard and a steaming bathhouse below

added.name: The Custody of the Vacated

contingents.what: custodians and porters who move bodies nobody is using

holds.name: the Long Hall of the Vacated, bed after bed

added.wantsFromYou: Discretion, and a fee to walk the Long Hall. If you have a claim on one of the sleepers, a paper that proves it.
added.offersYou: A body kept exactly as it was left, for as long as it is paid for, and the names of those who left them.
added.leverage: Every sleeper in the Long Hall has kin somewhere who would want to know. The Custody's whole trade depends on nobody asking.
added.whenBroken: The Long Hall's beds are opened, sleepers are carried home or buried, and a buyer in Dusklow stops paying for crates.
added.plainly: The custodians who keep the bodies Cogitants leave behind when they go into pure thought. They keep them well, for a fee, and they do not ask where the ones they sell are going.
added.descriptionSeed: When a Cogitant goes so far into thought that the body is only a place they used to be, the Custody takes it in. The Long Hall is quiet, clean and very long. The fees keep the beds warm, and the sleepers nobody pays for are sold, reasonably, to a buyer who never asks for a particular one.
added.appearance: A long cold hall of the Cogitarium, bed after bed of still sleepers under pale sheets, custodians in grey moving quietly between them with ledgers

feedsGM.through: bodies left by minds that will not return, kept and sold on

secretsGM: The Custody's best buyer is the Undercount's Dusklow fence (SNG-640). The Custodian believes she sells property its owners abandoned; she is not an agent (R40b.4).
The Cold Seal (SNG-642) was first made for the Long Hall.

added.name: The Grovehome Moot

contingents.what: Rootkin wardens of the Greenward, slow to muster and very hard to move once they have

holds.name: the thorned wall, grown on purpose

added.wantsFromYou: Patience. Bring a question to the Moot and wait for the answer, however long it takes. Bring an axe to the Eaves and do not come back.
added.offersYou: Grown shelter, fruit from trees older than your grandparents, and the Moot's word, which has never been broken because it has never been given quickly.
added.leverage: The Moot decides nothing in less than a season. Anything that has to be done faster, someone in the Quickwood will do without it, and the Moot will have to live with that.
added.whenBroken: The Heartroot's sealers win the argument, the Greenward closes, and the Quickwood stops keeping human hours.
added.plainly: The Rootkin's slow council at Grovehome. It keeps the Quickwood open to trade, and it has never decided anything in a hurry.
added.descriptionSeed: The Moot sits under the oldest trees in Grovehome and argues in seasons. It keeps the Quickwood's one door open to the world because trade requires it, and it keeps the Greenward thorned because the world requires that too. In the Heartroot, the argument to seal the wood is gaining ground.
added.appearance: A ring of seats grown from living roots under vast trees, Rootkin elders listening for a very long time, a thorned green wall at the edge of the wood

added.name: The Ceaseless

contingents.what: joyful builders who will not put their tools down

added.wantsFromYou: Your ground, to build on, and your hands, to build with. If you do not give them, they will build over what you have.
added.offersYou: Anything made, fast and beautifully, and a place on a scaffold that will never be finished.
added.leverage: They cannot stop, so they cannot hold what they build. Burn a scaffold under them and they will build on the ash instead of fighting you for it.
added.whenBroken: The Ceaseless scatter across the Making, each of them still building, and the Half-Cathedral gets finished by accident.
added.plainly: A cult of builders at the Making's pure pole who cannot stop and will not ask whether they should. They are joyful, and they build over anything in their way.
added.descriptionSeed: The Ceaseless build continuously, over each other, over the ground and over anything else that is there. Cinder Vael leads them, if leading is the word for being the one furthest ahead. They are not cruel. They simply do not see what they are building over.
added.appearance: A city of scaffolds built on scaffolds, builders singing as they work at every height, half-finished structures swallowing older half-finished structures

added.name: The Court of the Unfinished Plan

contingents.what: guild-wrights and scaffold crews working to the season's winning plan

added.wantsFromYou: An improvement. Bring the Court a better design for anything and it will listen. Bring it a finished thing and it will be politely sad for you.
added.offersYou: Wrights for any work, materials from the Forge-Eternal, and a seat at the next season's contest if your plan is good enough.
added.leverage: Whoever wins the season's contest governs until the next one. The Court is exactly as strong as its last plan, and everyone knows who is drafting the next.
added.whenBroken: The contest stops, the scaffolds come down, and the Ceaseless build over the Forge-Eternal before anyone has finished arguing.
added.plainly: The Making's governing contest. Each season the best plan wins, and whoever drew it governs until someone draws a better one.
added.descriptionSeed: The Wrights believe a finished thing has stopped being alive, so they govern the way they build: by improvement. Each season plans are laid before the Court, and the winner holds the Planmaster's office until a better one arrives. It is fair, it is glorious, and it is never done.
added.appearance: A hall of drafting tables under cathedral scaffolding, plans pinned over plans, Wrights arguing over a model with obvious delight

added.name: The Schedule of Pressureholt

contingents.what: maintenance crews, and the engine-guard who keep the Verge

holds.name: the Verge works under their precisely labelled tarpaulins

added.wantsFromYou: A slot. Everything in Pressureholt has a place in the Schedule, and so will you: when you arrive, what you want, and when you will leave.
added.offersYou: Repair for anything mechanical, passage through the Service Ways on a written route, and a Schedule that keeps its promises to the minute.
added.leverage: The Schedule is written down, all of it, and posted. Anyone who can read it can find the hour the Verge guard changes.
added.whenBroken: Pressureholt runs late for the first time in four centuries, and the Service Ways stop being mapped.
added.plainly: Pressureholt's government: a written specification for everything the city does, kept by the Chief of Schedule. It is warm, precise, and never late.
added.descriptionSeed: Pressureholt is a city that is also a machine, and the Schedule is its specification: every function, every shift, every failure mode written down and posted. The Enginewrights are warm people, and the Schedule is how they show it. It has no place for anything that was not planned.
added.appearance: A city of pipes and clock-faces, a great posted Schedule on a wall of brass plates, maintenance crews moving to the minute

added.name: The Long Choir

contingents.what: singers, most of them further away than they look

holds.name: the choir-house, as provisional as everything here

added.wantsFromYou: An hour of your listening, and then another. They will never force you. They will only keep asking, very gently, whether you would like to put the weight down.
added.offersYou: Peace, the quiet of a veil worn thin, and a song that makes the body's aches seem very far away.
added.leverage: The choir needs voices, and it loses them. Every singer who goes all the way into the song stops singing, so someone always has to be asked next.
added.whenBroken: The Thinning's song stops, some of its sleepers wake, and the Numen's pull weakens for a season.
added.plainly: A gentle choir at the Thinning that sings people toward letting go of their bodies. It has never forced anyone, and it is very good at asking.
added.descriptionSeed: The Long Choir sings where the veil is thin, and its song is kind. It asks, and asks again, whether you would not rather set the body down. Some singers go all the way in and do not come back. Their bodies stay behind, cared for, and in time someone comes to collect them.
added.appearance: A provisional wooden choir-house at the edge of a thin veil, robed singers with far-away eyes, a few still figures lying peacefully at the back

feedsGM.through: singers sung out of their bodies, and the bodies left behind

secretsGM: The Choirmaster is the Unbodied's agent; the choir is not (R40b.4). A kind power feeding a Sovereign is the lore's individually reasonable, cumulatively impossible.

added.name: Custodian Vantrel
added.title: First Custodian of the Vacated
added.role: First Custodian of the Vacated — keeps the bodies Cogitants leave behind, well and for a fee, and sells the unpaid ones to a buyer who never asks for a particular one
added.appearance: A thin, exact woman in custodian's grey, a ledger always under one arm, who looks at a sleeping body the way a clerk looks at an entry.
added.voiceHints: Quiet and procedural. Calls the sleepers the vacated and their bodies the property. Never raises her voice in the Long Hall.
added.wants: For the Long Hall to be kept well and paid for, and for nobody to confuse care with sentiment.
added.fears: A claimant at the door with a real paper for a body she has already sold.
knowledge: Who lies in every bed of the Long Hall, and who is paying for them
Which crates went to Dusklow, and on which nights

reactsToReputation.any: quotes you the fee before anything else
reactsToReputation.reliable: lets you walk the Hall without an escort
reactsToReputation.reckless: has the porters stand between you and the beds

questSeeds: A family arrives with a paper for a sleeper the Custody sold last spring
The Dusklow buyer has asked, for the first time, for a particular body
gear: a custodian's ledger bound in grey
added._domainsWhy: thought that has left the body, the quiet of the Hall, and the order of a ledger

added.name: Planmaster Wyncote
added.title: Planmaster of the Court of the Unfinished Plan
added.role: This season's Planmaster of the Making — won the contest with a better plan for the Half-Cathedral's north aisle, and governs until someone draws a better one
added.appearance: A cheerful man with graphite on both hands and a plan rolled under his arm, who keeps glancing up at the scaffolding as if it might have improved while he wasn't looking.
added.voiceHints: Quick and delighted. Interrupts himself with a better idea. Says 'not yet' where other people say 'no'.
added.wants: To be beaten at next season's contest by a plan so good he wishes he had drawn it.
added.fears: That the Ceaseless build over the Forge-Eternal before anyone has time to draw the next plan.
knowledge: Every plan laid before the Court for twenty seasons, and why each one lost
Where the Ceaseless will build next, roughly, and why he cannot stop them

reactsToReputation.reliable: shows you the plan for next season
reactsToReputation.reckless: asks you, kindly, not to touch the scaffolds

questSeeds: A plan has been laid before the Court that would finish the Half-Cathedral, and the Court does not know what to do with it
The Ceaseless have started building on Greenforge's timber yard
gear: a drafting case of well-used tools
added._domainsWhy: making that never finishes, the pattern in a plan, and stone that holds it up

added.name: Chief Kettering
added.title: Chief of Schedule of Pressureholt
added.role: Chief of Schedule — keeps Pressureholt's specification, which is to say keeps the city on time, and is warmer about it than anyone expects
added.appearance: A sturdy woman in a maintenance coat hung with small tools and a pocket watch on each side, who smiles when the hour strikes exactly.
added.voiceHints: Precise, friendly, and always gives a time. Asks you when you will be leaving before she asks your name, and means it kindly.
added.wants: A Schedule that has a slot for everyone, including the people it has not met yet.
added.fears: The thing in the Service Ways that is not on any Schedule, and the young ones who build outside it.
knowledge: The whole of the posted Schedule, and the parts that are not posted
Which Service Ways are mapped, and which only look it

reactsToReputation.any: gives you a slot and a time to leave
reactsToReputation.reckless: gives you a shorter one, and an escort

questSeeds: A shift has gone missing from the Verge guard, and the Schedule says it was never there
Gearheart has built something that is not in the specification, and it works
gear: two pocket watches, set a minute apart
added._domainsWhy: a city that is a machine, the order of the specification, and time kept to the minute
